implementation_summary: key-resolver.ts: added KeyResolver.removeServiceKey(service). It checks the service name, removes the keychain entry and ignores errors when no keychain is available. If the encrypted .qa-keys.json holds that account, it drops the entry and rewrites the file through the existing encrypted, serialized updateFallbackFile, so other entries are kept and the file is never written in plain text. If there is no entry, no file is created. SecretStore gained an optional delete(account). OsKeychainStore.delete uses Entry.deleteCredential or deletePassword when present, otherwise setPassword(''). Stores without delete are cleared with set(account, ''). The helper serviceAccount(service) is now exported, so it is also part of the @qa/core public API. beta.ts: SessionKeyResolver now overrides saveServiceKey, resolveServiceKey and removeServiceKey to use only the session secret store. They never touch the keychain, the file or environment variables, so a beta visitor never gets PAGESPEED_API_KEY. Saving or removing outside a session (or in a forgotten one) throws 'No session' and writes nothing. Empty keys and unknown service names are rejected.

handoff: Use KeyResolver.removeServiceKey('pagespeed') for AuditSettingsUpdate.pagespeedKey = null. After it runs, resolveServiceKey falls back to PAGESPEED_API_KEY or null. In beta mode, use the SessionKeyResolver instance: save, resolve and remove are session-only, never read env or disk, and throw 'No session' outside a request session. That makes it safe for a beta route to save service keys (ADR 0034 precondition). No migration or dependency change was made. Rollback: revert the two source files and delete the two test files.
